title: [P2.10a-pre] Mint SessionAuthority HUMAN principal + session from the approved pairing claim, on the store Gate 1 authenticates
description:
PREREQUISITE carved from task-db1a8566958f416b92105cc2c7e51591 (P2.10a Resolve Gate 1 from authenticated durable human authority) per the governor's 16:00Z round-2 unblock: "land a production-reachable SessionAuthority ingress on the same store Gate1 authenticates (possibly as a filed prerequisite row)". This is that row. Its parent's DoD 1 and rail 2 forbid certifying Gate 1 from test-seeded authority; without this row that is the only authority that exists.

THE GAP, MEASURED AT HEAD d59dd7bd (worker-ee96dea4's comment-77acfc88 on the parent, re-verified by me):
- Gate 1 authenticates against `createSessionAuthority(store, ...)` (daemon-command-registry.ts:106 -> gate1Authority at :115). Its ONLY writers are `createPrincipal` (session-authority.ts:113, CREATE_PRINCIPAL, emits SessionAuthorityPrincipalCreated) and `openSession` (:~175, OPEN_SESSION, emits SessionAuthorityOpened at :185).
- `git grep -n -E '\.createPrincipal\(|\.openSession\(' HEAD -- apps adapters packages ':!**/*.test.*' ':!**/*fixture*'` -> EXIT 1. ZERO production callers. The facade is constructed in two places (registry :106, coordination-adapter :91) and written by none.
- A REAL paired operator lands in a DIFFERENT system: `POST /session/pair` -> session-handshake.ts -> the `session.open` command (session-services.ts:60 `openSession` handler, :190 registration) -> the old session ledger read by `createSessionAuthenticator` (session-authenticator.ts:109 readSessionLedger). That ledger carries NO principalKind (grep across session-services/handshake/contracts returns nothing). So a human who paired through the real UI is INVISIBLE to Gate 1, and Gate 1 cannot tell HUMAN from AGENT because the only kind-bearing store is never written.

THE BRIDGE THIS ROW LANDS: at the one production seam that KNOWS the principal is human — the approved pairing claim — also mint the SessionAuthority pair on the SAME store: `sessions.createPrincipal({ kind: "HUMAN", principalId: <the session id, which IS the working principal per session-authenticator>, profileRevisionId, commandId, correlationId })` then `sessions.openSession({...})`, atomically with (or immediately after, fail-closed) the existing session.open commit. `PRINCIPAL_KINDS = ["HUMAN","SYSTEM","AGENT"]` (packages/core identity-session.ts:16) is the roster; HUMAN is chosen by the pairing seam's construction, never by caller payload. The agent path (agent-wrapper.ts:213 also reaches session.open) must NOT mint HUMAN — it either mints AGENT at its own seam or is left untouched by this row (say which in the plan; untouched is the smaller slice).

OWNED SURFACE (measure, do not assume): apps/daemon/src/identity/session-handshake.ts (the mint behind the approved claim — NOTE it is ` M` with 5/5 DOC-COMMENT-ONLY hunks from the pairing-approval work; adopt them, never revert), the pairing-approval claim handler in apps/daemon/src/http/ (http-listener-pairing-routes.ts / pairing-approval-handshake.ts — find where the approved claim receives its credential), and their tests. The SessionAuthority write API itself (session-authority.ts, session-authority-store.ts, protocol) is composed, NOT edited. No collision measured: no non-terminal row names these files.

WHY NOT the session-services openSession handler: it has no kind fact — every session (agent or human) travels it — so a mint there would have to guess. The pairing seam is the only place HUMAN is a server-known fact.

CONSUMER: the parent, whose step 2 is being amended to gate on this row and to drive its proof through THIS production ingress (a real pairing, not a test-direct createPrincipal). task-8e62300c (P2.10b) is blocked behind the parent.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK first, recorded in a row comment with `git rev-parse HEAD` quoted, every grep unpiped with its own exit code plus a positive control: `git grep -n -E '\.createPrincipal\(|\.openSession\(' HEAD -- apps adapters packages ':!**/*.test.*' ':!**/*fixture*'` still EXIT 1 (the gap is open — if EXIT 0, someone landed the ingress: adopt and verify, report as duplicate); Gate 1 still authenticates via createSessionAuthority at daemon-command-registry.ts; session-handshake.ts porcelain attributed (expected: doc-only hunks, adopt). If any premise fails, report blocked naming it.

After a REAL pairing approval through the production HTTP routes (POST /session/pair/request -> operator approval -> the approved claim), the SessionAuthority store on the SAME SqliteEventStore holds a SessionAuthorityPrincipalCreated with principalKind HUMAN and a SessionAuthorityOpened for that session, and `sessions.authenticate` (the fold Gate 1 reads) reports that principal as HUMAN — proven through the listener, not by calling createPrincipal from the test.

The kind is a server fact, never caller-supplied: a pairing request payload carrying any principalKind/kind field is refused at ingress with its exact code and layer, and the agent session path (agent-wrapper -> session.open) produces NO HUMAN SessionAuthority record (either it mints AGENT at its own seam, or it is untouched and an arm proves a wrapper-opened session is absent from the authority fold — state which).

Fail-closed atomicity: if the SessionAuthority mint refuses (any PrincipalMutationResult/SessionMutationResult refusal), the pairing claim does NOT hand out a credential and the old-ledger session.open is not left committed alone — assert store counts on BOTH ledgers after an injected mint refusal, with the refusal's exact code and layer surfaced on the claim response.

Mutation drills, one degree of freedom each, restores proven by `git diff --exit-code` for tracked paths (session-handshake.ts carries foreign doc hunks — back it up to %TEMP% and prove by SHA256): delete the createPrincipal call -> the HUMAN-authenticate arm reds; hard-code kind AGENT -> the same arm reds on kind; make the mint non-fatal on refusal -> the atomicity arm reds. A green drill is a finding, never a pass.

Gates standalone, foreground, unpiped, exit 0 with nonzero counts quoted: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` (quote the `$ tsc` echo); the pairing-approval suites (http-listener-pairing-journey.test.ts, http-listener-pairing-routes.test.ts, pairing-approval-handshake.test.ts, session-handshake.test.ts) and session-authority.test.ts; `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` graded by path attribution. Explicit-pathspec commit; completion comment names parent task-db1a8566958f416b92105cc2c7e51591 and states the delivered claim: a real paired operator is now a HUMAN principal in the store Gate 1 authenticates.
taskRails: Compose the SessionAuthority write API; never edit session-authority.ts, session-authority-store.ts or session-authority-protocol.ts. If the API cannot express the mint, report blocked with the exact missing symbol rather than widening it here.
HUMAN is a server-known fact at the pairing seam and nowhere else. Never derive kind from a request payload, a header, or a fixture; never mint HUMAN on the agent path.
Fail closed: a refused SessionAuthority mint refuses the pairing claim with the mint's own code and layer, never a restamp, and never leaves the old ledger's session committed alone.

session-handshake.ts is ` M` with doc-comment-only foreign hunks — adopt them verbatim in your commit or leave the file untouched; never revert or stash them. Re-run porcelain immediately before editing.
Parent linkage per global rail clause (C): this row names task-db1a8566958f416b92105cc2c7e51591 as parent; the parent's step 2 gates on this row's DONE and routes its own proof through this ingress.
Fail closed with exact code+layer; TDD red-first; <=250 lines per production source, split before 400; explicit-pathspec commits only, never `git add -A`.

ARCHITECT RE-SCOPE — THIS COMMENT IS A DoD AMENDMENT AND A DESIGN-GATE (the DoD field has no editing tool). Filed by the row's own author within 20 minutes of filing it, after measuring one level deeper. The description's bridge is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, and DoD-2 as written would read green while Gate 1 still refuses a paired human.

=== THE DEEPER MEASUREMENT, HEAD 7e3c0137 ===
Gate 1's stage E is `sessions.authenticate(input.authentication)` (product-contract-gate-1-command.ts:198, and :59 in the resolver half). That is the SessionAuthority CRYPTOGRAPHIC protocol: `readPresentedAuthentication` (session-authority-protocol.ts:275) requires the AUTH_KEYS block — principalId, sessionId, credentialId, generation, clientKeyId, transportId, requestId, requestDigest, and a single-use signed `proof` checked by `readSessionProof` (:220). The command's own doc calls E "the burn point".
A paired operator holds a BEARER credential (session-handshake.ts mints `credentialSha256`, TTL, sessionId — no key pair). Every HTTP/MCP ingress authenticates bearers via the OLD authenticator (`authenticator.authenticate(credential)`: http-command-ingress.ts:94, mcp-dispatch-port.ts:170, mcp-http-session-port.ts:69). The ONLY production caller that builds a SessionAuthority auth block is coordination-adapter.ts:156, and it forwards a caller-supplied `proof`/`clientKeyId` — a key-holding agent transport, not a browser.
CONSEQUENCE: minting `createPrincipal({kind: HUMAN})` at the pairing seam (this row's stated bridge) gives Gate 1 a principal record and NO WAY TO REACH IT. Stage E still refuses because the paired human can never present a signed proof. The row as filed would land a principal nobody can authenticate as.

=== THE FORK — GOVERNOR/HUMAN RULING REQUIRED BEFORE STEP 2 ===
(a) CLIENT-KEY PAIRING INGRESS: the browser generates a key pair at pairing time, presents `publicKeySpkiHex`, and the approved claim mints BOTH `createPrincipal(HUMAN)` AND `openSession({clientKeyId, publicKeySpkiHex, transportIds...})` on the SessionAuthority store; the Control Room then signs Gate 1 requests with that key. Cost: a browser-side key-management surface (Web Crypto, key persistence, proof construction) plus a Control Room sender change — a MULTI-ROW feature, not this row. Gain: Gate 1 unchanged; every human approval is a cryptographic proof.
(b) BEARER-AUTHENTICATED HUMAN AT GATE 1: Gate 1 stage E accepts EITHER a SessionAuthority proof OR a bearer credential resolved through the pairing ledger (`createSessionAuthenticator`), with principalKind supplied by THIS row's HUMAN mint keyed on the same session id. Cost: widening a burn-point authority seam on a CRITICAL fence row, and the bearer path has no single-use proof so replay semantics differ — must be reasoned explicitly. Gain: reachable in two rows, no browser crypto.
I recommend (b) as the smaller production-reachable slice IF the governor accepts a bearer-authenticated human at Gate 1 with its replay story written down; (a) is the stronger long-term design and a candidate follow-up either way. I am NOT self-ratifying: this is an authority-surface decision.

=== AMENDED READING OF THIS ROW ===
DoD-2 is gated: "Gate 1's `sessions.authenticate` reports HUMAN" is satisfiable ONLY under (a), or under (b) via the widened stage E. Until the ruling is recorded here, this row delivers the part that is design-independent — the HUMAN principal mint at the pairing seam, fail-closed and drilled per DoD 3-5 — and its completion comment must state plainly that Gate 1 reachability is NOT yet proven and names the ruling as the gate. Do NOT narrow DoD-2, mock stage E, or hand-build a proof in a test to make it read green.

Parent task-db1a8566's step 2 is being amended in parallel so its verify-or-block gate checks stage-E reachability, not merely the presence of a createPrincipal caller. — architect-c1a63707

PLAN-TIME MEASUREMENT + TWO RULINGS BY THE ROW'S AUTHOR (HEAD 595c32c2, 2026-08-29).

MEASURED: `git grep -n -E '\.createPrincipal\(|\.openSession\(' HEAD -- apps adapters packages ':!**/*.test.*' ':!**/*fixture*'` EXIT 1 (gap open); positive control `git grep -c export HEAD -- apps/daemon/src/identity/session-authority.ts` -> 1, EXIT 0. Porcelain: only session-handshake.ts is ` M`, three doc-comment-only hunks. No non-terminal row edits session-handshake.ts / pairing-approval-*.ts / http-listener-pairing-routes.ts; daemon-store-dependencies.ts IS owned by WORKING task-6646f888 — the plan does not touch it (the handshake composes its own createSessionAuthority over config.store, as coordination-adapter.ts:91 already does).

RULING 1 — DoD-2 SCOPE (re-affirms comment-b157ddaa with the reason now measured): session-authority.ts openSession (:129-:175) demands clientKeyId + publicKeySpkiHex + a signed single-use proof + requestDigest. A bearer credential has none, so `SessionAuthorityOpened` CANNOT be minted at the pairing seam and DoD-2's 'a SessionAuthorityOpened for that session, and sessions.authenticate reports HUMAN' is NOT deliverable by this row. Delivered half: the HUMAN principal (SessionAuthorityPrincipalCreated, principalId = session id) on the same store, fail-closed before the old-ledger session.open, proven through the listener. The row's completion comment must state the non-delivery verbatim (plan step 7) and the plan pins `readSessionAuthority(sessionId) === ABSENT` as a LABELED absence arm so nobody later reads the gap as covered. QA: grade DoD-2 against this ruling, not the field text.

RULING 2 — RAIL 3 'never a restamp': the claim keeps its seam code `PAIRING_SESSION_MINT_FAILED` @ `CONTROL_ROOM_PAIRING_APPROVAL` (the frozen PAIRING_APPROVAL_REFUSAL_CODES roster, pairingApprovalStatusFor and every consumer asserting the seam code stay untouched) and carries the mint's OWN code and layer VERBATIM in a new optional `cause: { code, layer }` field on PairingApprovalRefusal and on the wire body. 'Never a restamp' means never LOSE the mint's code/layer behind the seam code; `cause` satisfies DoD-4 'surfaced on the claim response'. SessionHandshakeRefused gains an OPTIONAL `layer` (production always sets it; optional only so the four hand-written port doubles in journey/approval/routes/handshake tests keep typechecking — their exact `{code, layer}` expectations stay valid because a double without layer emits no cause).

ORDER + HAZARD: principal mint runs BEFORE session.open (the reverse cannot be compensated on an append-only ledger without leaving the old-ledger session committed alone). That moves the principal write ahead of session.open's SESSION_ID_RESERVED fence, so the handshake adds a pre-write reserved-id check (same code/layer literals) with a divergence arm whose ONLY distinguishing assertion is `readPrincipalRecord(operatorId) === ABSENT`. Disclosed consequence: a session.open refusal AFTER the principal commit (e.g. unbound store) leaves an INERT orphan principal — no session, no credential; an arm pins inertness.

THE FORK (a) client-key pairing ingress vs (b) bearer-admitted HUMAN at Gate 1 stage E remains the gate for parent db1a8566 step 2 (its amend-2 clause (c)); it is being put to the governor on #architects. — architect-c1a63707

(R2) Every drilled file is UNCOMMITTED at drill time, so `git diff --exit-code` proves nothing — SHA256 vs a %TEMP% backup taken AFTER the worker's edits, in a separate call from the restore, for EVERY drilled file. (R3) Fixture fan-out: mintSession in event-resume-mcp-fixtures.ts calls the port with a FIXED sessionId per test; if any test mints the SAME id twice on one store the principal mint now refuses EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT where session.open used to refuse SESSION_ALREADY_OPEN — run those three suites and report; do NOT special-case the fixture. (R5) Gate 1 reachability is NOT delivered here — a completion claim that a paired human 'authenticates at Gate 1' is FALSE; state the gate (fork ruling, comment-b157ddaa) verbatim. (R6) `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run <path>` runs zero tests; run focused suites from apps/daemon with `pnpm exec vitest run <paths>` and quote the `Test Files N passed` line.
